findings: The APOB p.(Pro955Ser) variant shows defective LDL binding with a 44% reduction compared to controls
Functional analysis was performed in hepatocytes, which are relevant tissues for LDL metabolism
The study included controls from healthy individuals and comparisons with known pathogenic variants (p.(Arg3527Gln))
rationale: The variant demonstrates significantly reduced LDL uptake in hepatocytes compared to wild-type controls, with statistical significance (p<0.01). The population frequency (0.6%) is substantially lower than its prevalence in FH patients (9.8%), supporting pathogenicity.
experimental_details: LDL internalization efficiency was measured via fluorescence intensity after 30-min incubation at 37°C in hepatocytes. Comparisons were made between homozygous p.(Pro955Ser), heterozygous p.(Pro955Ser), pathogenic p.(Arg3527Gln), and healthy controls.
p1_source_location: Population frequency reported as 0.6% in text
p2_source_location: Variant prevalence of 9.8% in FH patients reported in text
